title: Distance on the Coordinate Plane
seo_title: Grade 8 Distance Between Two Points Worksheets: Pythagorean Theorem and Distance Formula
standard_text: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 distance worksheets: find the distance between two points by counting or with the Pythagorean theorem and the distance formula, find perimeters, compare distances and solve map problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Draw a right triangle: d = √(across² + up²).
key_sub: Same x or same y: just subtract. Otherwise square, add, then take the square root.
body_html:
Use the Pythagorean theorem

To find the distance between two points, draw a right triangle. The legs are how far across and how far up or down. The distance is the hypotenuse.

Distance formula: d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).

Example

Find the distance from (−2, 1) to (4, 9).

Across: 4 − (−2) = 6.

Up: 9 − 1 = 8.

d = √(36 + 64) = √100.

Answer: 10

If the points have the same x or the same y, just count (or subtract).

Common mistakes

  • Adding the legs: 3 + 4 is not the distance.
  • Forgetting the square root.
  • Subtracting a negative wrongly: 4 − (−2) = 6.
  • Mixing an x with a y.

faq.q: How do you find the distance between two points?
faq.a: Find how far across (x₂ − x₁) and how far up or down (y₂ − y₁). Then d = √(across² + up²). For (1, 1) and (4, 5): √(9 + 16) = 5.
d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). It is the Pythagorean theorem written with coordinates.

faq.q: What if the points are on the same horizontal line?
faq.a: Then the distance is just the difference of the x-coordinates (as a positive number).

faq.q: Can the distance be a square root?
faq.a: Yes. If the sum of squares is not a perfect square, the exact answer is a root like √34 ≈ 5.8.
